interest: Imperial ceremonies, coronation albums, and strained 1932 Emperor's birthday toasts in Chefoo and Tsingtao.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.001, covering Political Affairs: Japan, Chief Executive, Sovereign, Visits) consists of cross-reference sheets, accompanying despatches, and consular periodic report extracts dated between 1930 and 1939 relating to the Japanese Emperor and Imperial Household. The records include a February 1931 report from Tokyo concerning the anticipated birth of an imperial child and the traditional gochakutai (bandwearing) ceremony; April and May 1932 consular reports from Chefoo (Yantai) and Tsingtao (Qingdao) describing formal receptions hosted by Japanese consuls on Emperor Hirohito's birthday and noting the strained cordiality of participating Chinese officials amid growing Sino-Japanese tensions; an April 1930 despatch from American Ambassador William R. Castle, Jr. in Tokyo transmitting commemorative photograph albums of Emperor Hirohito's enthronement presented by the Imperial Coronation Office to former U.S. Ambassador Charles MacVeagh and Mrs. MacVeagh; and a March 1939 cross-reference slip relating to an 1868 diplomatic notification concerning the restoration of power to the Japanese Emperor during the Meiji Restoration.

subfiles.about: Reports on the celebration of Emperor Hirohito's birthday at the Japanese Consulate in Chefoo and the noticeable lack of cordiality from Chinese representatives.

subfiles.about: Details the Japanese Emperor's birthday reception in Tsingtao and rumors regarding the League of Nations Commission's visit.
